title: When the Playlist Turns
premise: Coral Crane, seventeen and de facto parent to his two younger siblings while their mom works hospital night shifts, has survived high school by being forgettable — until his music teacher pairs him with Priya Nair, his loudest nemesis, for a semester-long project archiving the neighborhood's disappearing vinyl shop. Digging through the shop's donated records, they uncover evidence that the building's slumlord landlord has been illegally evicting families, including Coral's own threatened apartment block. As the project becomes an underground campaign of mixtapes, testimony, and community organizing that the courts are too slow to touch, Coral must choose between staying safely invisible and standing up as the person his siblings already believe he is. The semester ends with the shop saved as a co-op, the landlord exposed, and Coral finally letting himself be seen — by Priya, by his classmates, and by himself.
about_author: O. M. Voss is a former after-school program coordinator who spent six years listening to teenagers explain why everything was fine. They write loud, hopeful stories about quiet kids from a small apartment full of borrowed records.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A chaotic morning — burnt toast, missing permission slips, little sister Junie's scraped knee — establishes Coral's invisible caretaker role before school. He keeps his head down in class, dodging attention. Emotional beat: weary competence masking exhaustion; the reader sees how much 'fine' costs him.

chapters.title: The Nemesis Clause
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Music teacher Mr. Okafor announces the semester project: document a local cultural landmark. To Coral's horror, he's paired with Priya Nair, who humiliated him freshman year and hasn't let him forget it. They're assigned the fading Corner Vinyl shop. Beat: dread sharpened by reluctant curiosity.

chapters.title: Dust and Static
chapters.summary: Alternating Coral/Priya POV. Their first visit to Corner Vinyl: owner Marisol Reyes shows them crates of donated records from evicted families who never came back for them. Priya is electric; Coral is guarded. Beat: friction, but the first crack of shared fascination.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Home life deepens: brother Des's silent struggles at school, mom's 3 a.m. returns, Coral cooking dinner he pretends isn't a big deal. A rent notice appears under the door. Beat: the stakes of home made concrete; Coral absorbs worry like it's his job.

chapters.title: B-Sides of You
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. We learn why Priya targets Coral: she remembers him as the boy who laughed when she froze during a recital. Working late in the shop, she catches him singing quietly to calm himself and realizes her nemesis file might be wrong. Beat: guilt and grudging respect.

chapters.title: The Eviction Box
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Archiving records, Coral finds a box labeled with his own street address — belongings from the Alvarez family, evicted last spring. Marisol mentions more boxes, more names, all tied to their landlord, Gerald Voss Realty. Beat: unease turning into recognition of a pattern.

chapters.title: Group Chat Ghosts
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya pulls school records and news clippings; Coral maps eviction dates against buildings Voss owns. They argue about what to do — report it? To whom? The district attorney's office already 'cleared' Voss twice. Beat: the law looks useless; anger finds its target.

chapters.title: Mixtape Manifesto
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. On impulse, Coral burns a CD of songs paired with the evicted families' stories and leaves copies around school anonymously. It spreads. Priya suspects him immediately but keeps his secret. Beat: Coral tastes agency for the first time — terrifying and addictive.

chapters.title: Junie Knows
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Nine-year-old Junie finds a copy of the mixtape and recognizes Coral's handwriting on the tracklist. Instead of telling Mom, she asks to help. Beat: Coral confronts the gap between the invisible self he performs and the hero his sister already sees.

chapters.title: Voss Comes Knocking
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. A 'property inspection' at Coral's building feels like intimidation; Voss's agent photographs the Cranes' apartment and mentions the 'troublemaking kids at the record store.' Coral goes pale and silent. Beat: the campaign acquires a face and a threat; fear enters the found family.

chapters.title: The Alliance of the Unnoticed
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Other students quietly join: the lunchroom ghost Theo, expelled-adjacent skater Bex, quiet genius Amara. Meetings happen inside Corner Vinyl after hours. Beat: belonging crystallizes — the misfits become a crew with a mission and a name: The Static.

chapters.title: Mom Finds Out
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Mom discovers Coral's involvement via a flyer with Junie's crayon additions. Instead of anger: shame that her son parented himself into this, and fear for their lease. She forbids it. Beat: heartbreak; Coral's protective role inverted — now he must protect her from worry.

chapters.title: Paper Trails
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Amara decodes the paper trail: forged inspection reports, a bribed city clerk. They need the original ledgers rumored to be stored in the shop's basement — Marisol's late husband kept meticulous books. Beat: hope with a deadline; the pieces exist if they can reach them.

chapters.title: Locked Doors
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The basement flooded years ago; the ledgers may be ruined. A tense, muddy salvage session yields waterlogged but legible pages. Coral and Priya nearly kiss amid the mildew and pull back. Beat: intimacy through shared risk; the romance line crosses from subtext toward text.

chapters.title: The Betrayal Beat
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Someone leaks the crew's plan to Voss's agent — Theo, whose brother works for the realty company and whose family's housing is leverage. Trust shatters; the group fractures. Beat: lowest midpoint; Coral retreats into invisibility, convinced caring was the mistake.

chapters.title: What Invisibility Costs
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. With the crew scattered, Voss fast-tracks the Cranes' eviction notice. Coral realizes silence never protected anyone — it just delayed the loss. He plays Mom the original mixtape and tells her everything. Beat: confession as reclamation; Mom, weeping, hands him back his purpose.

chapters.title: Forgive the Static
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Coral confronts Theo not with rage but with his story — the brother, the leverage, the fear. Theo agrees to testify and retrieve the signed bribe memo he saw. The crew reconvenes. Beat: forgiveness as strategy and grace; the found family repairs itself stronger.

chapters.title: Broadcast Night
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The plan: hijack the school's winter showcase livestream to air testimonies, the ledgers, and the mixtape. Everything that can go wrong does — equipment fails, a teacher nearly shuts it down. Beat: white-knuckle rising action; the whole neighborhood starts watching.

chapters.title: When the Playlist Turns
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Climax. Mid-broadcast, Voss arrives with lawyers demanding they stop; Coral steps in front of the camera — fully visible, name given — and tells the Alvarez family's story, then his own. Viewership explodes; a councilmember watching pledges an investigation live. Beat: courage as identity; the labels come off.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Track One
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Consequences cascade: state investigators open a case, Voss's licenses freeze, evictions halt pending review. Theo's brother cooperates. There's fallout at school — detention for the broadcast — accepted collectively. Beat: justice outside the law worked because the law finally followed; cost acknowledged.

chapters.title: Corner Store of Second Chances
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Resolution begins: Corner Vinyl converts to a community co-op with the crew as founding members; the Alvarez family moves back upstairs. Mom picks up a day shift. Coral and Priya finally finish the actual assignment — and admit the almost-kiss wasn't static. Beat: warmth, earned joy.

chapters.title: Loud, At Last
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Final scene: opening night at the co-op, Coral on a small stage introducing the permanent exhibit — the evicted families' records, playable by anyone. Junie in the front row, Mom off shift, Priya beside him. He sings, audibly, on purpose. Beat: belonging achieved; invisibility voluntarily retired.
